content_html:
Everyone agrees AI makes senior engineers more valuable. Almost nobody asks where the next generation of seniors is supposed to come from. The work AI automated away was never waste, it was the apprenticeship, and the hiring data says the bottom rung is already gone.

There's a story the industry loves telling right now: AI makes senior engineers more valuable. The people with judgment, the ones who can smell a bad design from the doorway, are the winners of this shift. It's a comforting story. It's even true.

It just has a hole in the middle big enough to drive a hiring freeze through. Seniors are not a renewable resource. Nobody arrives with fifteen years of scar tissue preinstalled. Every senior you've ever worked with started as a junior who got handed unglamorous work and spent years doing it. And AI has quietly eaten the exact work those years were made of.

This isn't a piece about whether AI writes good code. It writes plenty. It's about what happens to the supply of people who can tell.

Where Seniors Actually Come From

Ask a senior engineer what made them senior and you won't hear "a certification." You'll hear about systems they broke, incidents they sat through, codebases they had to read for weeks before anything made sense. Judgment isn't downloaded. It's accumulated through thousands of small collisions with real systems, most of them unglamorous, many of them boring at the time.

That's the part the "seniors win" narrative skips. It treats senior supply like weather, something that's just out there, replenishing itself. It isn't. It's manufactured. Slowly, expensively, by teams that gave someone a bottom rung to stand on and tolerated the wobble.

Your hiring plan probably assumes that when you need seniors in 2030, you'll hire them from the market. Fine. But the market is just other companies' former juniors. Someone, somewhere, has to be running the apprenticeship, or there's nothing to hire.

The Grunt Work Was the Curriculum

Think about what a junior developer's week actually looked like before AI tooling got good:

  1. Boilerplate - scaffolding CRUD endpoints and form validation taught the shape of the framework, where things live, what the conventions are and why they exist.
  2. Small bug fixes - the ticket nobody wanted taught you to read stack traces, then logs, then, crucially, other people's code. Not the code you'd write. The code that's actually there.
  3. Glue code - wiring service A to queue B taught how systems really connect: timeouts, retries, the config value that only matters in production.
  4. Tracing someone else's code - the "figure out why this happens" tasks built the mental model of the system that every future architecture decision would lean on.
  5. PR nitpicks - forty comments on your first pull request stung, and they were also the fastest taste-transfer mechanism the industry ever had.

Nobody defended this work. We called it toil, grunt work, the stuff you paid your dues on. So when AI showed up and started doing all of it in seconds, we celebrated. Finally, juniors can skip the boring parts and do the real engineering.

Except the boring parts were the training. An apprentice electrician spends years pulling cable and mounting boxes. Not because the master can't do it faster, but because that's how you learn how buildings actually work before anyone lets you near a panel that can kill you. Hand the cable-pulling to a robot and you still get wired buildings. You just stop getting electricians.

That's what the automation did. It didn't trim waste. It deleted the curriculum and kept the exam.

And it leaves today's juniors in a strange trap: with AI, they can produce more output than any junior in history, while collecting fewer reps than any junior in history. Output was never the point of junior work. The learning was the product; the tickets were just the delivery mechanism.

The Numbers Are Already In

This would be a hand-wavy think piece if the data weren't already showing it. It is, and from several independent directions.

SignalFire's State of Tech Talent report found that new graduates now make up just 7% of hires at Big Tech companies, with new grad hiring down more than 50% from pre-pandemic 2019 levels. The report also surfaced the quiet part said out loud: 37% of managers said they'd rather use AI than hire a Gen Z employee.

A Stanford team led by Erik Brynjolfsson analyzed payroll data from ADP, covering millions of workers, and found that early-career workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed occupations saw a 16% relative decline in employment since late 2022. Software engineering is one of the flagship examples. Meanwhile, workers 30 and over in those same occupations grew 6 to 12% through May 2025. Same jobs, opposite directions, split cleanly by age. A recession doesn't check your birth year. AI adoption apparently does.

The downstream effect is visible in graduate outcomes too: New York Fed data puts recent computer science grads at 6.1% unemployment, against a 4.8% average for recent graduates overall. The major an entire generation was told to pick now underperforms the average.

And the sentiment behind those numbers is not subtle. In survey data covered by Stack Overflow, 70% of hiring managers said they believe AI can do an intern's job, and 57% said they trust AI's output more than a recent grad's work.

The bottom rung isn't loosening. It's already off the ladder.

Rational for One, Starving for All

Here's the uncomfortable part: nobody in this story is making a mistake.

Run the math for a single team, this quarter. A junior hire costs a full salary plus a meaningful slice of a senior's week for a year or more before they're net positive, and then they might leave for a 30% raise somewhere else. An AI coding tool costs less than the team's coffee budget and is productive this afternoon. If you're the engineering manager with one open req and a delivery deadline, skipping the junior is the correct decision. Any CFO would sign off on it. Most do.

The problem is that everyone runs the same spreadsheet. Each company individually decides to hire seniors "from the market" instead of growing them, and the market is nothing but the output of other companies' junior programs. Skipping juniors is free-riding on someone else's apprenticeship. It works beautifully right up until it's universal.

This is a commons problem, and the senior pool of 2031 is the commons. No single company owns it, no single company is punished for depleting it this quarter, and no line item on anyone's P&L represents it.

The lag is what makes it dangerous. The juniors not hired in 2025 are the mid-level engineers who won't exist in 2028 and the seniors who won't exist in 2031. And a missing cohort can't be backfilled later, because the thing you'd be hiring is years of accumulated judgment. You can raise a salary band in one budget cycle. You can't raise experience.

"Maybe AI Just Becomes the Senior"

The honest counterargument deserves a fair hearing, because it's not stupid. It goes like this: models are improving fast, so by the time the senior gap arrives, AI will be doing the senior work too. Worrying about the junior pipeline is like worrying about horse-stable capacity in 1910 while Ford ramps up the assembly line.

Take it seriously, and it still breaks on one stubborn fact: someone has to put their name on the merge.

When an AI-generated migration takes down production at 2 a.m., "the model did it" is not an incident report anyone accepts. Not your customers, not your auditors, not the regulator if you're in fintech or healthcare. Accountability is load-bearing in software organizations, and it can't be delegated to a system that can't be fired, deposed, or promoted. Some human reviews the output, approves it, and answers for it.

And review is not a checkbox. Reviewing well means knowing which diffs are risky and which are routine, what the blast radius of a schema change is, when the tests are green because the code is right versus green because they don't test the failure mode. That's judgment. It's precisely the thing the apprenticeship used to produce, in exactly the people we've stopped training.

So the "AI becomes the senior" future eats its own premise: the more code AI writes, the more the human job becomes review, and the industry is currently betting on that skill while dismantling the only machine known to produce it.

The Stanford data has a wrinkle that backs this up: employment held or grew in roles where AI augments people, and workers who used AI to learn and validate their work fared better than those who delegated whole tasks to it. The market is already sorting people, not by whether they use AI, but by whether they use it in a way that builds judgment or replaces it.

Keeping the Apprenticeship Alive

You can't fix industry-wide hiring incentives from your desk. What you can control is whether learning still happens inside the work you and your team already have.

If you're early in your career:

  • Struggle first, prompt second. Give every problem a genuine attempt before you ask the model. The struggle is not an inefficiency to optimize away; it's the mechanism that writes the lesson into your head. AI is a phenomenal tutor when it explains something you already fought with, and a lesson-shredder when it answers before you've formed the question.
  • Read every AI diff like a reviewer, because you are one. As far as git blame and your team are concerned, you wrote that code. If you can't explain a line in the diff, you're not done. Make understanding the deliverable, not the merge.
  • Do some things the slow way, on purpose. Trace the framework call by hand once. Write the migration yourself before asking for one. You're not being a purist, you're doing reps, the same way athletes still lift weights even though forklifts exist.
  • Get good at review early. Review is where the job is heading. Volunteer for it, study how the best reviewer on your team comments, and learn to articulate why something is risky. That skill compounds faster than raw output ever will.

If you lead a team:

  • Hire one junior, with an actual plan. Not as charity, and not as a body for ticket throughput. A plan: rotations through subsystems, a named mentor with time carved out, attendance at incident reviews. One deliberately-grown junior beats zero on principle and beats three unsupported ones in practice.
  • Assign understanding, not just output. Have them present how the payment flow works end to end. Put them on the on-call shadow rotation. Ask them to write the postmortem draft. None of this ships features, and all of it manufactures the thing you'll be desperate to hire in five years.
  • Keep the instructive tickets human. Not the soul-crushing ones. Automate those with a clear conscience. But the gnarly little bug in the legacy module that forces someone to actually read the system? That ticket is tuition. Don't spend it on the model.
  • Review AI usage together. Look at prompts and diffs in pairs, the way you'd pair on code. How a junior uses the model is their process now; if it's invisible, so are their gaps.

None of this shows up in this quarter's velocity. That's the point. The apprenticeship never showed up in velocity either, which is exactly why it was so easy to automate away without anyone noticing what it was.

The industry didn't decide to stop producing seniors. It automated the thing that produced them, one perfectly rational quarter at a time. The teams that have enough seniors in five years will be the ones that never stopped making them.

sentences.zh: 小错误修复 - 没有人想要的票教你阅读堆栈跟踪，然后记录日志，然后，最重要的是，其他人的代码。

sentences.en: Not the code you'd write.
sentences.zh: 不是您要编写的代码。

sentences.en: The code that's actually there.
sentences.zh: 实际存在的代码。

blocks.html_en: • Glue code - wiring service A to queue B taught how systems really connect: timeouts, retries, the config value that only matters in production.

sentences.en: Glue code - wiring service A to queue B taught how systems really connect: timeouts, retries, the config value that only matters in production.
sentences.zh: 粘合代码 - 将服务 A 连接到队列 B 教导系统如何真正连接：超时、重试、仅在生产中重要的配置值。

blocks.html_en: • Tracing someone else's code - the "figure out why this happens" tasks built the mental model of the system that every future architecture decision would lean on.

sentences.en: Tracing someone else's code - the "figure out why this happens" tasks built the mental model of the system that every future architecture decision would lean on.
sentences.zh: 追踪别人的代码——“弄清楚为什么会发生这种情况”任务构建了系统的心理模型，未来的每个架构决策都将依赖该模型。

blocks.html_en: • PR nitpicks - forty comments on your first pull request stung, and they were also the fastest taste-transfer mechanism the industry ever had.

sentences.en: PR nitpicks - forty comments on your first pull request stung, and they were also the fastest taste-transfer mechanism the industry ever had.
sentences.zh: 公关挑剔 - 对你的第一个拉取请求的四十条评论刺痛了，它们也是业界有史以来最快的品味转移机制。

blocks.html_en: Nobody defended this work. We called it toil, grunt work, the stuff you paid your dues on. So when AI showed up and started doing all of it in seconds, we celebrated. Finally, juniors can skip the boring parts and do the real engineering.

sentences.en: Nobody defended this work.
sentences.zh: 没有人为这项工作辩护。

sentences.en: We called it toil, grunt work, the stuff you paid your dues on.
sentences.zh: 我们称其为辛劳、繁重的工作、你付出代价的东西。

sentences.en: So when AI showed up and started doing all of it in seconds, we celebrated.
sentences.zh: 因此，当人工智能出现并开始在几秒钟内完成所有工作时，我们庆祝了。

sentences.en: Finally, juniors can skip the boring parts and do the real engineering.
sentences.zh: 最后，初级人员可以跳过枯燥的部分并进行真正的工程设计。

blocks.html_en: Except the boring parts were the training. An apprentice electrician spends years pulling cable and mounting boxes. Not because the master can't do it faster, but because that's how you learn how buildings actually work before anyone lets you near a panel that can kill you. Hand the cable-pulling to a robot and you still get wired buildings. You just stop getting electricians.

sentences.en: Except the boring parts were the training.
sentences.zh: 除了无聊的部分就是训练。

sentences.en: An apprentice electrician spends years pulling cable and mounting boxes.
sentences.zh: 一名学徒电工花费数年时间拉动电缆和安装盒。

sentences.en: Not because the master can't do it faster, but because that's how you learn how buildings actually work before anyone lets you near a panel that can kill you.
sentences.zh: 不是因为大师不能更快地做到这一点，而是因为这样你就可以在任何人让你靠近可能杀死你的面板之前了解建筑物的实际工作原理。

sentences.en: Hand the cable-pulling to a robot and you still get wired buildings.
sentences.zh: 将拉缆的工作交给机器人，你仍然可以连接建筑物。

sentences.en: You just stop getting electricians.
sentences.zh: 你就不再找电工了。

blocks.html_en: That's what the automation did. It didn't trim waste. It deleted the curriculum and kept the exam.

sentences.en: That's what the automation did.
sentences.zh: 这就是自动化所做的。

sentences.en: It didn't trim waste.
sentences.zh: 它没有减少浪费。

sentences.en: It deleted the curriculum and kept the exam.
sentences.zh: 它删除了课程并保留了考试。

blocks.html_en: And it leaves today's juniors in a strange trap: with AI, they can produce more output than any junior in history, while collecting fewer reps than any junior in history. Output was never the point of junior work. The learning was the product; the tickets were just the delivery mechanism.

sentences.en: And it leaves today's juniors in a strange trap: with AI, they can produce more output than any junior in history, while collecting fewer reps than any junior in history.
sentences.zh: 这让今天的初级选手陷入了一个奇怪的陷阱：有了人工智能，他们可以比历史上任何初级选手产生更多的产出，同时比历史上任何初级选手获得更少的代表次数。

sentences.en: Output was never the point of junior work.
sentences.zh: 产出从来都不是初级工作的重点。

sentences.en: The learning was the product; the tickets were just the delivery mechanism.
sentences.zh: 学习就是产品；门票只是传递机制。

blocks.html_en: The Numbers Are Already In

sentences.en: The Numbers Are Already In
sentences.zh: 数字已在

blocks.html_en: This would be a hand-wavy think piece if the data weren't already showing it. It is, and from several independent directions.

sentences.en: This would be a hand-wavy think piece if the data weren't already showing it.
sentences.zh: 如果数据还没有显示出来的话，这将是一个令人费解的想法。

sentences.en: It is, and from several independent directions.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，而且来自几个独立的方向。

blocks.html_en: SignalFire's State of Tech Talent report found that new graduates now make up just 7% of hires at Big Tech companies, with new grad hiring down more than 50% from pre-pandemic 2019 levels. The report also surfaced the quiet part said out loud: 37% of managers said they'd rather use AI than hire a Gen Z employee.

sentences.en: SignalFire's State of Tech Talent report found that new graduates now make up just 7% of hires at Big Tech companies, with new grad hiring down more than 50% from pre-pandemic 2019 levels.
sentences.zh: SignalFire 的科技人才状况报告发现，目前大型科技公司的应届毕业生仅占员工总数的 7%，较 2019 年疫情爆发前的水平下降了 50% 以上。

sentences.en: The report also surfaced the quiet part said out loud: 37% of managers said they'd rather use AI than hire a Gen Z employee.
sentences.zh: 该报告还指出了沉默的部分：37% 的经理表示，他们宁愿使用人工智能，也不愿雇用 Z 世代员工。

blocks.html_en: A Stanford team led by Erik Brynjolfsson analyzed payroll data from ADP, covering millions of workers, and found that early-career workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed occupations saw a 16% relative decline in employment since late 2022. Software engineering is one of the flagship examples. Meanwhile, workers 30 and over in those same occupations grew 6 to 12% through May 2025. Same jobs, opposite directions, split cleanly by age. A recession doesn't check your birth year. AI adoption apparently does.

sentences.en: A Stanford team led by Erik Brynjolfsson analyzed payroll data from ADP, covering millions of workers, and found that early-career workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed occupations saw a 16% relative decline in employment since late 2022.
sentences.zh: 由 Erik Brynjolfsson 领导的斯坦福大学团队分析了 ADP 涵盖数百万工人的工资数据，发现自 2022 年底以来，从事 AI 暴露程度最高的职业、年龄在 22 岁至 25 岁之间的早期职业工人的就业率相对下降了 16%。

sentences.en: Software engineering is one of the flagship examples.
sentences.zh: 软件工程是旗舰示例之一。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, workers 30 and over in those same occupations grew 6 to 12% through May 2025.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，到 2025 年 5 月，从事相同职业的 30 岁及以上工人数量增长了 6% 至 12%。

sentences.en: Same jobs, opposite directions, split cleanly by age.
sentences.zh: 相同的工作，相反的方向，按年龄划分。

sentences.en: A recession doesn't check your birth year.
sentences.zh: 经济衰退不会检查你的出生年份。

sentences.en: AI adoption apparently does.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的采用显然是这样的。

blocks.html_en: The downstream effect is visible in graduate outcomes too: New York Fed data puts recent computer science grads at 6.1% unemployment, against a 4.8% average for recent graduates overall. The major an entire generation was told to pick now underperforms the average.

sentences.en: The downstream effect is visible in graduate outcomes too: New York Fed data puts recent computer science grads at 6.1% unemployment, against a 4.8% average for recent graduates overall.
sentences.zh: 下游效应在毕业生成果中也很明显：纽约联邦储备银行的数据显示，应届计算机科学毕业生的失业率为 6.1%，而应届毕业生的总体失业率为 4.8%。

sentences.en: The major an entire generation was told to pick now underperforms the average.
sentences.zh: 整整一代人被告知要选择的专业现在表现低于平均水平。

blocks.html_en: And the sentiment behind those numbers is not subtle. In survey data covered by Stack Overflow, 70% of hiring managers said they believe AI can do an intern's job, and 57% said they trust AI's output more than a recent grad's work.

sentences.en: And the sentiment behind those numbers is not subtle.
sentences.zh: 这些数字背后的情绪并不微妙。

sentences.en: In survey data covered by Stack Overflow, 70% of hiring managers said they believe AI can do an intern's job, and 57% said they trust AI's output more than a recent grad's work.
sentences.zh: 在 Stack Overflow 的调查数据中，70% 的招聘经理表示，他们相信人工智能可以完成实习生的工作，57% 的人表示，他们更信任人工智能的输出，而不是应届毕业生的工作。

blocks.html_en: The bottom rung isn't loosening. It's already off the ladder.

sentences.en: The bottom rung isn't loosening.
sentences.zh: 底部横档没有松动。

sentences.en: It's already off the ladder.
sentences.zh: 已经从梯子上下来了。

blocks.html_en: Rational for One, Starving for All

sentences.en: Rational for One, Starving for All
sentences.zh: 一个人的理性，一个人的饥饿

blocks.html_en: Here's the uncomfortable part: nobody in this story is making a mistake.

sentences.en: Here's the uncomfortable part: nobody in this story is making a mistake.
sentences.zh: 这是令人不舒服的部分：这个故事中没有人犯错误。

blocks.html_en: Run the math for a single team, this quarter. A junior hire costs a full salary plus a meaningful slice of a senior's week for a year or more before they're net positive, and then they might leave for a 30% raise somewhere else. An AI coding tool costs less than the team's coffee budget and is productive this afternoon. If you're the engineering manager with one open req and a delivery deadline, skipping the junior is the correct decision. Any CFO would sign off on it. Most do.

sentences.en: Run the math for a single team, this quarter.
sentences.zh: 本季度对单个团队进行数学计算。

sentences.en: A junior hire costs a full salary plus a meaningful slice of a senior's week for a year or more before they're net positive, and then they might leave for a 30% raise somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 初级员工的聘用费用是全额工资，加上高级员工一周的有意义的工作时间，为期一年或更长时间，然后他们可能会在其他地方加薪 30%。

sentences.en: An AI coding tool costs less than the team's coffee budget and is productive this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 人工智能编码工具的成本低于团队的咖啡预算，并且今天下午就很有成效。

sentences.en: If you're the engineering manager with one open req and a delivery deadline, skipping the junior is the correct decision.
sentences.zh: 如果您是工程经理，有一个开放请求和交付期限，那么跳过初级职位是正确的决定。

sentences.en: Any CFO would sign off on it.
sentences.zh: 任何首席财务官都会签署该协议。

sentences.en: Most do.
sentences.zh: 大多数都是这样。

blocks.html_en: The problem is that everyone runs the same spreadsheet. Each company individually decides to hire seniors "from the market" instead of growing them, and the market is nothing but the output of other companies' junior programs. Skipping juniors is free-riding on someone else's apprenticeship. It works beautifully right up until it's universal.

sentences.en: The problem is that everyone runs the same spreadsheet.
sentences.zh: 问题是每个人都运行相同的电子表格。

sentences.en: Each company individually decides to hire seniors "from the market" instead of growing them, and the market is nothing but the output of other companies' junior programs.
sentences.zh: 每家公司都单独决定“从市场上”聘用高级人才，而不是培养他们，而市场只不过是其他公司初级项目的产出。

sentences.en: Skipping juniors is free-riding on someone else's apprenticeship.
sentences.zh: 跳过青少年组就是搭别人学徒的便车。

sentences.en: It works beautifully right up until it's universal.
sentences.zh: 在普及之前，它的工作效果非常好。

blocks.html_en: This is a commons problem, and the senior pool of 2031 is the commons. No single company owns it, no single company is punished for depleting it this quarter, and no line item on anyone's P&L represents it.

sentences.en: This is a commons problem, and the senior pool of 2031 is the commons.
sentences.zh: 这是一个公地问题，2031年的高级池就是公地。

sentences.en: No single company owns it, no single company is punished for depleting it this quarter, and no line item on anyone's P&L represents it.
sentences.zh: 没有任何一家公司拥有它，没有任何一家公司因本季度耗尽它而受到惩罚，任何人的损益表上都没有任何项目代表它。

blocks.html_en: The lag is what makes it dangerous. The juniors not hired in 2025 are the mid-level engineers who won't exist in 2028 and the seniors who won't exist in 2031. And a missing cohort can't be backfilled later, because the thing you'd be hiring is years of accumulated judgment. You can raise a salary band in one budget cycle. You can't raise experience.

sentences.en: The lag is what makes it dangerous.
sentences.zh: 滞后使得它变得危险。

sentences.en: The juniors not hired in 2025 are the mid-level engineers who won't exist in 2028 and the seniors who won't exist in 2031.
sentences.zh: 2025年未聘用的初级工程师是2028年将不存在的中级工程师，以及2031年将不存在的高级工程师。

sentences.en: And a missing cohort can't be backfilled later, because the thing you'd be hiring is years of accumulated judgment.
sentences.zh: 而且缺失的团队以后无法填补，因为你要雇用的是多年积累的判断力。

sentences.en: You can raise a salary band in one budget cycle.
sentences.zh: 您可以在一个预算周期内提高工资范围。

sentences.en: You can't raise experience.
sentences.zh: 你无法提升经验。

blocks.html_en: "Maybe AI Just Becomes the Senior"

sentences.en: "Maybe AI Just Becomes the Senior"
sentences.zh: “也许人工智能只是成为高级”

blocks.html_en: The honest counterargument deserves a fair hearing, because it's not stupid. It goes like this: models are improving fast, so by the time the senior gap arrives, AI will be doing the senior work too. Worrying about the junior pipeline is like worrying about horse-stable capacity in 1910 while Ford ramps up the assembly line.

sentences.en: The honest counterargument deserves a fair hearing, because it's not stupid.
sentences.zh: 诚实的反驳应该得到公平的听证，因为它并不愚蠢。

sentences.en: It goes like this: models are improving fast, so by the time the senior gap arrives, AI will be doing the senior work too.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的：模型正在快速改进，因此当高级差距到来时，人工智能也将承担高级工作。

sentences.en: Worrying about the junior pipeline is like worrying about horse-stable capacity in 1910 while Ford ramps up the assembly line.
sentences.zh: 担心初级管道就像 1910 年福特扩大装配线时担心马厩的产能一样。

blocks.html_en: Take it seriously, and it still breaks on one stubborn fact: someone has to put their name on the merge.

sentences.en: Take it seriously, and it still breaks on one stubborn fact: someone has to put their name on the merge.
sentences.zh: 认真对待它，它仍然违背了一个顽固的事实：必须有人在合并上署上自己的名字。

blocks.html_en: When an AI-generated migration takes down production at 2 a.m., "the model did it" is not an incident report anyone accepts. Not your customers, not your auditors, not the regulator if you're in fintech or healthcare. Accountability is load-bearing in software organizations, and it can't be delegated to a system that can't be fired, deposed, or promoted. Some human reviews the output, approves it, and answers for it.

sentences.en: When an AI-generated migration takes down production at 2 a.m., "the model did it" is not an incident report anyone accepts.
sentences.zh: 当人工智能生成的迁移在凌晨 2 点停止生产时，“模型做到了”并不是任何人都会接受的事件报告。

sentences.en: Not your customers, not your auditors, not the regulator if you're in fintech or healthcare.
sentences.zh: 如果您从事金融科技或医疗保健行业，则不是您的客户，不是您的审计师，也不是监管机构。

sentences.en: Accountability is load-bearing in software organizations, and it can't be delegated to a system that can't be fired, deposed, or promoted.
sentences.zh: 责任在软件组织中是重担，不能将其委托给一个不能被解雇、废黜或晋升的系统。

sentences.en: Some human reviews the output, approves it, and answers for it.
sentences.zh: 一些人审查输出，批准它，并回答它。

blocks.html_en: And review is not a checkbox. Reviewing well means knowing which diffs are risky and which are routine, what the blast radius of a schema change is, when the tests are green because the code is right versus green because they don't test the failure mode. That's judgment. It's precisely the thing the apprenticeship used to produce, in exactly the people we've stopped training.

sentences.en: And review is not a checkbox.
sentences.zh: 评论不是一个复选框。

sentences.en: Reviewing well means knowing which diffs are risky and which are routine, what the blast radius of a schema change is, when the tests are green because the code is right versus green because they don't test the failure mode.
sentences.zh: 良好的审查意味着知道哪些差异是有风险的，哪些是常规的，模式更改的爆炸半径是多少，测试何时是绿色的，因为代码是正确的，而绿色的，是因为它们不测试故障模式。

sentences.en: That's judgment.
sentences.zh: 这就是判断。

sentences.en: It's precisely the thing the apprenticeship used to produce, in exactly the people we've stopped training.
sentences.zh: 这正是学徒期所产生的东西，正是我们停止培训的人身上产生的东西。

blocks.html_en: So the "AI becomes the senior" future eats its own premise: the more code AI writes, the more the human job becomes review, and the industry is currently betting on that skill while dismantling the only machine known to produce it.

sentences.en: So the "AI becomes the senior" future eats its own premise: the more code AI writes, the more the human job becomes review, and the industry is currently betting on that skill while dismantling the only machine known to produce it.
sentences.zh: 因此，“人工智能成为高级”的未来有其自身的前提：人工智能编写的代码越多，人类的工作就越容易受到审查，而该行业目前正在押注于这项技能，同时拆除已知的唯一能够生产这种技能的机器。

blocks.html_en: The Stanford data has a wrinkle that backs this up: employment held or grew in roles where AI augments people, and workers who used AI to learn and validate their work fared better than those who delegated whole tasks to it. The market is already sorting people, not by whether they use AI, but by whether they use it in a way that builds judgment or replaces it.

sentences.en: The Stanford data has a wrinkle that backs this up: employment held or grew in roles where AI augments people, and workers who used AI to learn and validate their work fared better than those who delegated whole tasks to it.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福大学的数据有一个事实支持了这一点：在人工智能增强人类能力的岗位上，就业机会得以保持或增长，而使用人工智能来学习和验证自己工作的员工比那些将全部任务委托给人工智能的员工表现更好。

sentences.en: The market is already sorting people, not by whether they use AI, but by whether they use it in a way that builds judgment or replaces it.
sentences.zh: 市场已经在对人们进行分类，不是根据他们是否使用人工智能，而是根据他们是否以建立判断或取代判断的方式使用人工智能。

blocks.html_en: Keeping the Apprenticeship Alive

sentences.en: Keeping the Apprenticeship Alive
sentences.zh: 保持学徒制的活力

blocks.html_en: You can't fix industry-wide hiring incentives from your desk. What you can control is whether learning still happens inside the work you and your team already have.

sentences.en: You can't fix industry-wide hiring incentives from your desk.
sentences.zh: 您无法在办公桌上制定全行业的招聘激励措施。

sentences.en: What you can control is whether learning still happens inside the work you and your team already have.
sentences.zh: 您可以控制的是学习是否仍然发生在您和您的团队已有的工作中。

blocks.html_en: If you're early in your career:

sentences.en: If you're early in your career:
sentences.zh: 如果您处于职业生涯早期：

blocks.html_en: • Struggle first, prompt second. Give every problem a genuine attempt before you ask the model. The struggle is not an inefficiency to optimize away; it's the mechanism that writes the lesson into your head. AI is a phenomenal tutor when it explains something you already fought with, and a lesson-shredder when it answers before you've formed the question.

sentences.en: Struggle first, prompt second.
sentences.zh: 先奋斗，后行动。

sentences.en: Give every problem a genuine attempt before you ask the model.
sentences.zh: 在询问模型之前，对每个问题都进行真正的尝试。

sentences.en: The struggle is not an inefficiency to optimize away; it's the mechanism that writes the lesson into your head.
sentences.zh: 这种斗争并不是为了优化而导致效率低下，而是因为效率低下。它是将教训写入你脑海的机制。

sentences.en: AI is a phenomenal tutor when it explains something you already fought with, and a lesson-shredder when it answers before you've formed the question.
sentences.zh: 当人工智能解释你已经遇到过的问题时，它是一位非凡的导师；当它在你提出问题之前就给出答案时，它就是一个教训粉碎机。

blocks.html_en: • Read every AI diff like a reviewer, because you are one. As far as git blame and your team are concerned, you wrote that code. If you can't explain a line in the diff, you're not done. Make understanding the deliverable, not the merge.

sentences.en: Read every AI diff like a reviewer, because you are one.
sentences.zh: 像审稿人一样阅读每个 AI 差异，因为你就是其中之一。

sentences.en: As far as git blame and your team are concerned, you wrote that code.
sentences.zh: 就 git Blame 和您的团队而言，您编写了该代码。

sentences.en: If you can't explain a line in the diff, you're not done.
sentences.zh: 如果您无法解释差异中的一行，那么您就没有完成。

sentences.en: Make understanding the deliverable, not the merge.
sentences.zh: 理解可交付成果，而不是合并。

blocks.html_en: • Do some things the slow way, on purpose. Trace the framework call by hand once. Write the migration yourself before asking for one. You're not being a purist, you're doing reps, the same way athletes still lift weights even though forklifts exist.

sentences.en: Do some things the slow way, on purpose.
sentences.zh: 有目的地慢慢地做一些事情。

sentences.en: Trace the framework call by hand once.
sentences.zh: 手动跟踪框架调用一次。

content_html_zh:
每个人都同意人工智能让高级工程师更有价值。 几乎没有人问下一代老年人应该来自哪里。 人工智能自动化的工作从来都不是浪费，而是学徒期，而招聘数据显示，底层已经消失了。

业界现在喜欢讲一个故事：人工智能让高级工程师更有价值。 那些有判断力的人，那些从门口就能闻到糟糕设计的人，是这一转变的赢家。 这是一个令人安慰的故事。 这甚至是真的。

它只是中间有一个足够大的洞来推动招聘冻结。 老年人不是可再生资源。 没有人在到达时就已经预先安装了十五年的疤痕组织。 与你共事过的每一位前辈都是从初级员工开始的，他们接受了乏味的工作，并花费了数年的时间来完成它。 人工智能已经悄然蚕食了那些年的工作。

这不是一篇关于人工智能是否能写出好的代码的文章。 写得还蛮多的。 这是关于有能力的人的供应会发生什么。

老年人实际上来自哪里

询问高级工程师是什么让他们成为高级工程师，你不会听到“认证”。 你会听到他们破坏的系统、他们经历的事件、他们必须阅读数周的代码库才能让一切变得有意义。 判决未下载。 它是通过与真实系统的数千次小碰撞而积累起来的，其中大多数是平淡无奇的，其中许多在当时是无聊的。

这是“老年人获胜”叙述中跳过的部分。 它对待高级供给就像对待天气一样，是一种随处可见、可以自我补充的东西。 事实并非如此。 它是制造出来的。 慢慢地、昂贵地，团队给了某人一个底层的立足点并容忍了摇摆。

您的招聘计划可能假设，当您在 2030 年需要老年人时，您将从市场上雇用他们。 美好的。 但市场只是其他公司的前辈。 必须在某个地方有人来管理学徒期，否则就没有什么可雇佣的。

繁重的工作就是课程

想想在人工智能工具变得优秀之前，初级开发人员的一周实际上是什么样子的：

  1. 样板文件 - 脚手架 CRUD 端点和表单验证教会了框架的形状、事物存在的位置、约定是什么以及它们存在的原因。
  2. 小错误修复 - 没有人想要的票教你阅读堆栈跟踪，然后记录日志，然后，最重要的是，其他人的代码。 不是您要编写的代码。 实际存在的代码。
  3. 粘合代码 - 将服务 A 连接到队列 B 教导系统如何真正连接：超时、重试、仅在生产中重要的配置值。
  4. 追踪别人的代码——“弄清楚为什么会发生这种情况”任务构建了系统的心理模型，未来的每个架构决策都将依赖该模型。
  5. 公关挑剔 - 对你的第一个拉取请求的四十条评论刺痛了，它们也是业界有史以来最快的品味转移机制。

没有人为这项工作辩护。 我们称其为辛劳、繁重的工作、你付出代价的东西。 因此，当人工智能出现并开始在几秒钟内完成所有工作时，我们庆祝了。 最后，初级人员可以跳过枯燥的部分并进行真正的工程设计。

除了无聊的部分就是训练。 一名学徒电工花费数年时间拉动电缆和安装盒。 不是因为大师不能更快地做到这一点，而是因为这样你就可以在任何人让你靠近可能杀死你的面板之前了解建筑物的实际工作原理。 将拉缆的工作交给机器人，你仍然可以连接建筑物。 你就不再找电工了。

这就是自动化所做的。 它没有减少浪费。 它删除了课程并保留了考试。

这让今天的初级选手陷入了一个奇怪的陷阱：有了人工智能，他们可以比历史上任何初级选手产生更多的产出，同时比历史上任何初级选手获得更少的代表次数。 产出从来都不是初级工作的重点。 学习就是产品；门票只是传递机制。

数字已在

如果数据还没有显示出来的话，这将是一个令人费解的想法。 确实如此，而且来自几个独立的方向。

SignalFire 的科技人才状况报告发现，目前大型科技公司的应届毕业生仅占员工总数的 7%，较 2019 年疫情爆发前的水平下降了 50% 以上。 该报告还指出了沉默的部分：37% 的经理表示，他们宁愿使用人工智能，也不愿雇用 Z 世代员工。

由 Erik Brynjolfsson 领导的斯坦福大学团队分析了 ADP 涵盖数百万工人的工资数据，发现自 2022 年底以来，从事 AI 暴露程度最高的职业、年龄在 22 岁至 25 岁之间的早期职业工人的就业率相对下降了 16%。 软件工程是旗舰示例之一。 与此同时，到 2025 年 5 月，从事相同职业的 30 岁及以上工人数量增长了 6% 至 12%。 相同的工作，相反的方向，按年龄划分。 经济衰退不会检查你的出生年份。 人工智能的采用显然是这样的。

下游效应在毕业生成果中也很明显：纽约联邦储备银行的数据显示，应届计算机科学毕业生的失业率为 6.1%，而应届毕业生的总体失业率为 4.8%。 整整一代人被告知要选择的专业现在表现低于平均水平。

这些数字背后的情绪并不微妙。 在 Stack Overflow 的调查数据中，70% 的招聘经理表示，他们相信人工智能可以完成实习生的工作，57% 的人表示，他们更信任人工智能的输出，而不是应届毕业生的工作。

底部横档没有松动。 已经从梯子上下来了。

一个人的理性，一个人的饥饿

这是令人不舒服的部分：这个故事中没有人犯错误。

本季度对单个团队进行数学计算。 初级员工的聘用费用是全额工资，加上高级员工一周的有意义的工作时间，为期一年或更长时间，然后他们可能会在其他地方加薪 30%。 人工智能编码工具的成本低于团队的咖啡预算，并且今天下午就很有成效。 如果您是工程经理，有一个开放请求和交付期限，那么跳过初级职位是正确的决定。 任何首席财务官都会签署该协议。 大多数都是这样。

问题是每个人都运行相同的电子表格。 每家公司都单独决定“从市场上”聘用高级人才，而不是培养他们，而市场只不过是其他公司初级项目的产出。 跳过青少年组就是搭别人学徒的便车。 在普及之前，它的工作效果非常好。

这是一个公地问题，2031年的高级池就是公地。 没有任何一家公司拥有它，没有任何一家公司因本季度耗尽它而受到惩罚，任何人的损益表上都没有任何项目代表它。

滞后使得它变得危险。 2025年未聘用的初级工程师是2028年将不存在的中级工程师，以及2031年将不存在的高级工程师。 而且缺失的团队以后无法填补，因为你要雇用的是多年积累的判断力。 您可以在一个预算周期内提高工资范围。 你无法提升经验。

“也许人工智能只是成为高级”

诚实的反驳应该得到公平的听证，因为它并不愚蠢。 事情是这样的：模型正在快速改进，因此当高级差距到来时，人工智能也将承担高级工作。 担心初级管道就像 1910 年福特扩大装配线时担心马厩的产能一样。

认真对待它，它仍然违背了一个顽固的事实：必须有人在合并上署上自己的名字。

当人工智能生成的迁移在凌晨 2 点停止生产时，“模型做到了”并不是任何人都会接受的事件报告。 如果您从事金融科技或医疗保健行业，则不是您的客户，不是您的审计师，也不是监管机构。 责任在软件组织中是重担，不能将其委托给一个不能被解雇、废黜或晋升的系统。 一些人审查输出，批准它，并回答它。

评论不是一个复选框。 良好的审查意味着知道哪些差异是有风险的，哪些是常规的，模式更改的爆炸半径是多少，测试何时是绿色的，因为代码是正确的，而绿色的，是因为它们不测试故障模式。 这就是判断。 这正是学徒期所产生的东西，正是我们停止培训的人身上产生的东西。

因此，“人工智能成为高级”的未来有其自身的前提：人工智能编写的代码越多，人类的工作就越容易受到审查，而该行业目前正在押注于这项技能，同时拆除已知的唯一能够生产这种技能的机器。

斯坦福大学的数据有一个事实支持了这一点：在人工智能增强人类能力的岗位上，就业机会得以保持或增长，而使用人工智能来学习和验证自己工作的员工比那些将全部任务委托给人工智能的员工表现更好。 市场已经在对人们进行分类，不是根据他们是否使用人工智能，而是根据他们是否以建立判断或取代判断的方式使用人工智能。

保持学徒制的活力

您无法在办公桌上制定全行业的招聘激励措施。 您可以控制的是学习是否仍然发生在您和您的团队已有的工作中。

如果您处于职业生涯早期：

  • 先奋斗，后行动。 在询问模型之前，对每个问题都进行真正的尝试。 这种斗争并不是为了优化而导致效率低下，而是因为效率低下。它是将教训写入你脑海的机制。 当人工智能解释你已经遇到过的问题时，它是一位非凡的导师；当它在你提出问题之前就给出答案时，它就是一个教训粉碎机。
  • 像审稿人一样阅读每个 AI 差异，因为你就是其中之一。 就 git Blame 和您的团队而言，您编写了该代码。 如果您无法解释差异中的一行，那么您就没有完成。 理解可交付成果，而不是合并。
  • 有目的地慢慢地做一些事情。 手动跟踪框架调用一次。 在请求迁移之前自己编写迁移。 你不是一个纯粹主义者，你只是在做重复动作，就像运动员在叉车存在的情况下仍然举重一样。
  • 尽早做好复习。 审查是工作的方向。 自愿参与其中，研究团队中最好的审阅者如何评论，并学会阐明为什么某些事情是有风险的。 这种技能的复合速度比原始输出更快。

如果你领导一个团队：

  • 雇用一名初级员工，并制定实际计划。 不是作为慈善机构，也不是作为门票吞吐量的机构。 计划：子系统轮换、指定时间导师、参加事件审查。 一名刻意培养的少年在原则上击败了零，并在实践中击败了三名无支持的少年。
  • 分配理解，而不仅仅是输出。 让他们演示支付流程是如何端到端运作的。 将他们安排在待命的影子轮换中。 请他们写一份尸检草稿。 这些产品都没有任何功能，但所有这些产品都制造出你在五年内迫切需要的东西。
  • 保持指导性门票的人性化。 而不是那些摧残灵魂的人。 让那些问心无愧的人自动化。 但是遗留模块中的棘手小错误迫使人们真正阅读系统？ 这张票就是学费。 不要把钱花在模型上。
  • 一起回顾人工智能的使用情况。 成对查看提示和差异，就像在代码上配对一样。 后辈如何使用模型，现在就是他们的过程；如果它是看不见的，那么它们的间隙也是看不见的。

这些都没有体现在本季度的速度中。 这就是重点。 学徒期也从未以速度出现，这正是为什么它如此容易被自动化而没有人注意到它是什么的原因。

该行业并未决定停止生产老年人。 它将生产它们的事情自动化了，一次一个完全理性的季度。 五年内拥有足够高年级球员的球队将是那些从未停止过培养高年级球员的球队。
